newsitem.title: UK: S&P gives Gothaer Rueck claims-paying rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P gives Gothaer Rueck claims-paying rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it assigned its BBB minus claims-paying ability rating to Gothaer Rueckversicherung AG (Gothaer Rueck).
"The rating reflects privileged access to good business from German mutuals, a well-diversified book by line of business and a conservative investment philosophy," S&P said in a statement.
"Offsetting these strengths are a somewhat undeveloped financial strategy, a mixed track-record with a poor operating performance and weak capital until 1994," S&P said.
S&P said it also has some general concerns about the long-term position of smaller reinsurers in Germany as they are forced to adapt to an increasingly liberalised and competitive marketplace.

-- Gothaer Rueck is a small domestic reinsurer with 1.06 billion marks in gross premiums and 93 million marks in published equity. It is the internal reinsurer of Gothaer Group, whose main life and nonlife entities are Gothaer Lebensversicherung AG ranking 18th domestically and Gothaer Versicherungsbank ranking 5th domestically.

"S&P considers access to group business to be a key strength. Additionally, the mutual character of the Gothaer Group should continue, in practice, to give the company privileged access to third-party business from small and medium-sized mutual insurers, usually on a quota-share basis," S&P said.

-- Gothaer Rueck enjoys a well-diversified book by line of business: life (37.0 percent), motor (40.2 percent of nonlife premium income), fire (19.5 percent), general third-party liability (8.1 percent), personal accident (3.4 percent), marine (3.0 percent), and other classes (25.8 percent, mostly engineering, comprehensive building and, to a lesser extent, legal expenses and credit). Business is well-balanced between personal and commercial lines, although essentially domestic.

-- Investment philosophy is expected to remain conservative with a strong emphasis on security and liquidity. However, the company's financial strategy is still somewhat undeveloped. Gothaer Rueck relies heavily on investment income and there few earnings benchmark beyond a required three percent return on net premiums.

-- Operating performance has been disappointing over the 1990-1994 period. This is reflected in an average combined ratio of 109.4 percent, although this was mostly attributable to an adverse loss development caused by reciprocal and U.S. businesses assumed until 1993 and the subsequent reserve strengthening. Operating losses, combined with a strong growth in net premiums at the beginning of the decade, resulted in weakened capitalization although the position has improved since 1994 with the completion of the reserve strengthening exercise. Operating performance was restored in 1995 with a combined ratio down to 103.4 percent from 112.4 percent and, given the relative absence of industrial business, S&P expects the improvement to continue in 1996.

Going forward, S&P said it expects the company to post adequate underwriting results now that the reserve strengthening exercise has been completed. Moderate premium growth and improved earnings should help capital to remain adequate. However, S&P said it believes that the onus is now on management to show that they can adapt and perform successfully in the rapidly evolving German and international reinsurance sector, Standard & Poor's said.
